proposals.before: Yelu Xidi was descended from the Prince of Chu on his mother's side.
proposals.after: Yelu Xidi was a descendant of the Prince of Chu of the Mengfu (Meng Father) lineage.
proposals.reason: 孟父 is a Khitan Yelu lineage term (Meng Father line), not "mother's side".

proposals.before: Yelu Xidi was a descendant of the Prince of Chu on his mother's side.
proposals.after: Yelu Xidi was a descendant of the Prince of Chu of the Mengfu lineage.
proposals.reason: Same error as idiomatic: 孟父 ≠ maternal side.

proposals.before: The empress dowager agreed and added the titles Golden Purple Glory Grandee and Inspector Grand Preceptor.
proposals.after: The empress dowager agreed and added the titles Golden Purple Glory Grandee and Inspector Grand Commandant.
proposals.reason: 太尉 is Grand Commandant/Grand Marshal, not Grand Preceptor (太傅).

proposals.before: The empress dowager followed this and added the titles Golden Purple Glory Grandee and Grand Preceptor on inspection.
proposals.after: The empress dowager followed this and added the titles Golden Purple Glory Grandee and Inspector Grand Commandant.
proposals.reason: 太尉 misread as Grand Preceptor.

proposals.before: He answered, "Each morning I recite the precepts left by Taizu, Taizong, and my forebears; I have had no time for Buddhism."
proposals.after: He answered, "Each morning I recite the precepts left by Taizu, Taizong, and my late forebear; I have had no time for Buddhism."
proposals.reason: 先臣 is singular (Xiuge), not plural forebears.

proposals.before: Yelu Xuegu, whose courtesy name was Yixin, was a grandson by a concubine of the Yuyue Wa.
proposals.after: Yelu Xuegu, whose courtesy name was Yixinyin, was a grandson by a concubine of the Yuyue Wa.
proposals.reason: 乙辛隱 is three characters; Yixin drops 隱.

decisions.after: Yelu Xidi was a descendant of the Prince of Chu of the Mengfu lineage.
decisions.reason: 孟父楚國王之後 names the Mengfu (eldest-uncle) Yelu lineage, not maternal descent; the proposed fix is right in substance, but the parenthetical '(Meng Father)' is awkward in idiomatic English.
孟父 is the Mengfu lineage label, not 'mother's side'; the proposed 'Prince of Chu of the Mengfu lineage' restores the correct sense of 孟父楚國王之後.
檢校太尉 is Inspector Grand Commandant; 太尉 is not Grand Preceptor (太傅), so the proposed title is the accurate repair.
檢校太尉 means Inspector Grand Commandant; rendering 太尉 as Grand Preceptor and 'on inspection' misreads both 太尉 and 檢校.
先臣 is singular for the speaker's late father/forebear-minister, not plural 'forebears'; 'my late forebear' matches 先臣遺訓.
字乙辛隱 is the three-character courtesy name Yixinyin; 'Yixin' omits 隱 and is incomplete.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0006 shows English Yixin came only from dropping 隱 in 乙辛隱; the courtesy-name claim must read Yixinyin while zh, pinyin, id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence stay the same.
